title: Supervised Fine-Tuning & Instruction Following
oneLineScope: Taking a pretrained base language model and continuing its training on curated instruction–response demonstrations — the step that turns a text predictor into an instruction follower.

diagrams.caption: The supervised fine-tuning pipeline: a pretrained base LM and an instruction–response dataset feed a cross-entropy training step, producing an instruction-following model. A muted dashed arrow continues to a greyed 'next: RLHF' box, marking that step as out of scope.
diagrams.altText: A left-to-right pipeline. Two inputs on the left: a blue 'Pretrained base LM (weights θ₀)' box and an 'instruction → response dataset' box containing two example pairs. Both feed into a red 'Supervised fine-tuning' box (labeled with cross-entropy loss on instruction–response pairs). An arrow exits to a green 'Instruction-following model (θ′)' box, annotated with 'e.g. FLAN (Wei et al. 2021)' and 'InstructGPT SFT stage (Ouyang et al. 2022)'. A dashed grey arrow continues from that box to a muted dashed 'next: RLHF (out of scope here)' box on the far right.
diagrams.prompt: Structural pipeline diagram flowing left to right. On the left, two input boxes stacked vertically: (top) a blue-outlined box labeled 'Pretrained base LM' with sub-label '(weights θ₀)'; (bottom) a box labeled 'Dataset' containing two rows each showing an 'instruction' box pointing with a right-arrow to a green 'response' box, and annotated 'demonstrations of desired behavior'. Arrows from both input boxes converge into a central red-outlined box labeled 'Supervised fine-tuning' with sub-labels 'cross-entropy loss on instruction–response pairs' and the formula 'ℒ(θ) = −∑ log P_θ(response | instruction)'. An arrow exits right to a green-outlined box labeled 'Instruction-following model (θ′)' annotated 'e.g. FLAN (Wei et al. 2021)' and 'InstructGPT SFT stage (Ouyang et al. 2022)'. From that box, a dashed grey arrow leads to a muted grey dashed-outline box on the far right labeled 'next: RLHF (out of scope here)' with annotation 'human feedback + RL'. Label every element.

bibliography.citation: Wei, J., et al. (2021). "Finetuned Language Models are Zero-Shot Learners." ICLR 2022.
bibliography.annotation: The FLAN paper. §3 describes the instruction-tuning setup: 62 tasks rephrased as natural-language instructions, fine-tuned on a 137B LM. §4 reports the zero-shot generalization improvement on held-out task clusters. The clearest demonstration that broad instruction-tuning teaches a general capability, not narrow task memorization. Read §2–4 for the core result.

bibliography.citation: Ouyang, L., et al. (2022). "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback." NeurIPS 35.
bibliography.annotation: The InstructGPT paper. §3.1 describes the SFT stage: human contractor demonstrations, cross-entropy fine-tuning of GPT-3. §3.2–3.3 describe the subsequent RLHF stages — those are out of scope here but useful to scan to understand why SFT alone is not the end of the story. §4 gives the human-evaluation results comparing SFT, RLHF, and the raw base model.

bibliography.citation: Liang, P., et al. (2022). "Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)." TMLR.
bibliography.annotation: Benchmarks instruction-following models (including InstructGPT variants) on a wide range of tasks with consistent evaluation methodology. Useful for seeing what SFT-trained models can and cannot do in practice, and for calibrating claims about the generalization benefit of instruction-tuning. §4–5 cover the evaluation dimensions most relevant here.
